thread.title: 2 Industries Where Apple Could Buy Up Other Companies

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: 2 Industries Where Apple Could Buy Up Other Companies
text:
Apple By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 27, 2018 12:14 p.m. ET Maybe you think Apple is an iPhone company with a services business. Or maybe it’s a services company with an iPhone business. Either way, when you buy one you get the other.
And services are undoubtedly crucial to Apple’s (AAPL) growth. Investors understand this: Earlier this month, we explored the possibility of an Amazon.com (AMZN) Prime-like bundle that combines music, video and news . And on Thursday, an analyst went even further, suggesting that the company could use mergers and acquisitions to dive more deeply into gaming and automotive services.
“With increasing focus on services revenues, particularly in the form of subscriptions, Apple’s interest in entering new end-markets is likely to be evaluated based on the opportunity for Apple to offer services (leveraging the iOS platform) on a large installed base,” JP Morgan ’s Samik Chatterjee wrote.
Chatterjee initiated coverage of the company with an “overweight” rating and a $292 price target that is the second-highest on Wall Street, according to FactSet, and $8 below Monnes Crespi Hardt’s high. The company’s shares were up about 2% Thursday morning.
Newsletter Sign-up So what should Apple buy? Chatterjee suggested a few ideas, though he didn’t specifically say any one company was a likely takeout target.
Videogames, he said, are a large and growing industry moving toward digital distribution, which would suit Apple—particularly, Chatterjee wrote, with the growth in smartphone-based gaming.
“Apple’s focus on services will be highly complemented by videogames, which are taking time and monetization share from other forms of entertainment,” he wrote.
JP Morgan Chase And while Chatterjee doesn’t necessarily see the company becoming a car maker—even if some people might like that —he does wonder if it might look at other manufacturers that would help it create better experiences in consumers’ cars.
That, he suggested, could mean “infotainment” companies—the likes of Alpine Electronics or Visteon (VC)—or smaller ones that could give Apple “experience in integration of software-based services with the hardware.” ( Barron’s has mentioned Visteon as a possible Apple target before.)
Recommended Reading An Apple Media ‘Bundle’ Worth $37 Billion? Is Apple Underinvesting in Innovation? Apple’s Video Ambition: Will It Be iPhone-Only? Apple, Chatterjee wrote, has historically been hardware-heavy in its M&A. But, he wrote, “as we look at the transformation of the business to services at a rapid pace, we expect a greater bias toward acquiring subscription-based software businesses that can be integrated into the Services segment.”
Chatterjee’s price target is almost 30% above current levels and roughly 25% higher than Factset’s mean Wall Street target. JP Morgan had been without an analyst covering Apple for about a year.
